title: As much as you can
hookLine: be mindful of Allah as much as you are able (64:16)
last: HE GUIDES THE HEART THROUGH IT.

lines: UP AT FIVE. GYM EVERY DAY.
A COMMAND, AND FOUR MORE WORDS.
cards: New Year's resolutions have a well-known shelf life. Up at five every day. Gym seven days a week.
A book a week. Never eat sugar again. By February, many are gone, and often the person feels worse than if they'd never started.

The plan was too big to carry, so they carried none of it. Near its end, Surah At-Taghabun gives a command that sounds almost like a correction to that habit. It asks for everything, then adds four words.

teach.h: MASTATA'TUM: AS FAR AS YOU ARE ABLE.
teach.b: Verse sixteen. Pickthall: "So keep your duty to Allah as best ye can". In Arabic: fattaqu llaha mastata'tum.

Be mindful of God, as much as you are able. The verse goes on: listen, and obey, and spend; that's better for yourselves. Commentators set it beside a verse in Surah Al 'Imran: be mindful of God as he deserves to be.

Some early scholars thought this verse eased the earlier one. Many others said the two explain each other: God deserves complete mindfulness, and what he asks of each person is that, within their real capacity.

teach.h: NO SOUL TASKED BEYOND ITS SCOPE.
teach.b: Pickthall: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." The hadith makes it practical.

teach.h: DO OF IT AS MUCH AS YOU CAN.
teach.b: Bukhari and Muslim record the Prophet ﷺ saying: when I forbid you something, avoid it; when I command you something, do of it as much as you can.
Another report in Bukhari says the deeds most loved by God are the ones done consistently, even if small. Put those together and you get a very different plan from a New Year's resolution.
Not everything at once, then nothing. As much as you can, then keep going. The sick person prays sitting; if not sitting, lying down.
The traveler shortens. The one who can't fast makes it up later or feeds the poor. Islamic law is full of these adjustments, and they all stand on this phrase.
As much as you can isn't an excuse for doing less. It's the measure that lets you keep doing it.

how: Islamic law builds many concessions on this principle: the sick may pray sitting or lying down, travelers shorten prayers, and those unable to fast make up the days or feed the poor; many Muslims also favor small, steady devotions.

o: to be excused from a hard duty
to be able, to have the capacity
to try your hardest, past all limits

games.q: as much as you can — tap the pairs.
p: as far as you are able
no soul tasked beyond its scope
do as much of it as you can

s: 'as much as you can' means doing less is always fine
it's the measure that lets you keep going, not an excuse.
the sick person may pray sitting, or lying down
Islamic law adjusts worship to real capacity.
the Prophet said the most loved deeds are the biggest ones
the most loved are the most constant, even if small.

games.q: the Prophet gives a command. you can't do all of it. what does the hadith say?
o: then you're excused from all of it.
do as much of it as you can.
wait until you can do it perfectly.
games.why: when I command you something, do of it as much as you can; when I forbid something, avoid it.

practice: Think of one good intention you've let fall because it was too big: daily prayer, exercise, reading, calling home. Shrink it to a size you could truly do every day, even on a bad day: five minutes, one page, one call a week.
Picture doing that small version tomorrow, and the day after, and let your breath be easy, just as much as it is.

wordCard.voice: Istata'a: to have the capacity, the ability behind Surah At-Taghabun's command to be mindful of God as much as you are able. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: so be mindful of God as much as you are able. istata'a means to be able, to have the capacity.

carryVoice: Your line: done consistently, even if small. Small and steady outlasts big and brief. Day six hundred thirty-one.
